title: 3.7.18 Lab: Build a New Object with Spread + Override
description: Use object spread to copy an object with one property overridden and one property added, leaving the original untouched. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the base object
steps.instructions: The starter gives you an object with three properties (the lesson calls it settings; you may rename it): const settings = { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14, wrap: true }; Leave its keys and values as they are.

steps.title: Copy with one property overridden
steps.instructions: Use object spread to build a copy of settings (the lesson calls it changed; use any name that fits), with one existing property changed. The override must be written after the spread.

steps.title: Copy with a new property added
steps.instructions: Use object spread again to build a second copy (the lesson calls it extended), with a new property that settings did not have.

steps.title: Log all three objects
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print both copies and the original settings object. Confirm the original is unchanged.

requirements.title: Object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Declare an object in braces with at least three name: value pairs.

requirements.title: Object spread used
requirements.description: Uses object spread, written as ... inside an object literal. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Spread is three dots in front of an object, written inside the braces of a new object.

requirements.title: Override after the spread
requirements.description: Writes a property after the spread so the override wins. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Write the property you want to change AFTER the spread: { ...settings, fontSize: 18 }. The later entry wins.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: changed overrides one value of settings, extended adds one key, and settings is unchanged
requirements.description: After the code runs, settings is still { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14, wrap: true }, changed overrides one of its values, extended adds one new key, and the output shows both copies. Help: 3.7.15 (Copying an Object with Changes)
requirements.hint: Build each copy with object spread ({ ...settings, fontSize: 18 }) and print all three. Never assign into settings itself.

checks.expr: changed !== null && typeof changed === 'object' && Object.keys(changed).some(($k) => changed[$k] !== settings[$k])
checks.fail: changed has the same values as settings: the override did not win. Write it AFTER the spread, { ...settings, fontSize: 18 }; a property written before the spread is replaced by the copied one.
changed should have the same three keys as settings (theme, fontSize, wrap), with one of their values changed. Adding a new key is what extended is for.
changed should change exactly one of settings' values.

checks.expr: extended !== null && typeof extended === 'object' && Object.keys(settings).every(($k) => $k in extended && (extended[$k] === settings[$k] || (changed !== null && typeof changed === 'object' && extended[$k] === changed[$k])))
checks.fail: extended should keep theme, fontSize and wrap from the object it spreads (settings, or changed): { ...settings, language: "en" }.
extended should add exactly ONE new key that settings does not have.
checks.failExpr: 'extended should add exactly ONE new key that settings does not have; it adds ' + Object.keys(extended).filter(($k) => !($k in settings)).length + '.'

requirements.title: changed and extended are spread from settings and printed by code that runs
requirements.description: When settings holds other values, the values changed and extended copy from it change too, and console.log calls that run print both copies and settings. Help: 3.7.15 (Copying an Object with Changes)
requirements.hint: Build both copies with { ...settings, ... } and print changed, extended and settings. An object typed in by hand, or typed-in output, does not change when settings does.

checks.fail: changed has to be copied from settings with spread: when the checker changes the values in settings, the values changed keeps from it must change too. An object typed in by hand stays the same.
extended has to be copied from settings with spread: when the checker changes the values in settings, the values extended keeps from it must change too. An object typed in by hand stays the same.
Print changed and extended with console.log calls that run. Typed-in text does not count.
Print settings too, console.log(settings), so the output shows the original did not change.
Build changed with object spread too: { ...settings, fontSize: 18 }. Object.assign does the same job but is not this lab's tool.
